notes: Criminal burglary appeal; Mrs. Eaves' boarding house is merely the crime scene (defendant entered a lodger's private room to steal), with no discussion of the legality or character of room-letting.

Zoning-validity dispute over a single owner's tract restricted to single-family residential use versus commercial rezoning; no lodger/boarder or short-term-letting practice is at issue, only rental of the house as an ordinary single-family residence.
Dispute over ownership of proceeds from leasing a federal cotton acreage allotment under a cash farm lease of grazing land; unrelated to letting of dwellings or rooms.

Purely procedural zoning dispute over whether the City Commission could amend zoning to an apartment district without a prior Plan Commission recommendation; never reaches the substance of lodging or boarding-house regulation.

Stock-fraud rescission suit; rental income from the conveyed property's furnished apartments and rent houses is discussed only as a measure of damages, not as a subject of legal characterization or regulation.
Personal-injury/invitee-licensee premises-liability suit against a commercial parking garage operator; no lodging or letting issue present.

notes: Zoning-validity case about a commercial apartment-hotel development rather than an individual householder's short-term letting; characterization left null because the court classifies the zoning district, not the occupancy arrangement (lease/license/lodging/innkeeping). Majority upheld the apartment hotel rezoning (favorable to multi-family letting); the dissent's quotation of Euclid v. Ambler framing apartment houses as quasi-nuisances is the clearest adverse-doctrine material, hence 'mixed'.

Hotel-guest property-theft suit addressing innkeeper liability limits under Art. 4592 (covering 'hotel, apartment hotel or boarding house keeper') and lock/door demonstrative-evidence issues; the statute is invoked only for its civil liability-limitation function, not the legality or character of letting practice.

holding_summary: Appellant sued for a declaratory judgment that he held a verbal lifetime lease on a suite of hotel rooms he and his wife had occupied for years at $500 a month, after making substantial improvements to the rooms. The trial court directed a verdict against him, and the appellate court affirmed, holding the evidence failed to establish an unambiguous offer and acceptance of a lifetime lease and that, even if such an agreement existed, it would only have created a tenancy at will terminable by either party.

notes: Involves a commercial hotel letting rooms for long-term (years, claimed lifetime) residential occupancy rather than short-term lodging; duration_of_occupancy set to 'unclear' because the actual occupancy at issue (years/lifetime) does not map to the nights/weeks/months categories. Marked favorable because the court treats hotel-room letting for pay as capable of creating an ordinary (if only at-will) tenancy, an incident of the hotel's business, even though the specific lifetime claim failed for lack of proof.
Adverse-possession/title dispute over farmland turning on a rice-farming tenancy and secret-entry doctrine; the tenancy discussed is agricultural, not residential room- or house-letting.

Rescission/fraud suit over an exchange of real estate that included a tourist court business ('Tangelo Courts'); the case turns on misrepresentations about income, water supply, and sewerage, not on the legal character or regulation of short-term lodging itself.

Priority dispute over rents assigned as loan security and impounded during foreclosure, where the tenant was a commercial car dealership (Western Olds Company); no residential letting or lodging issue.

Heirship and cotenant adverse-possession title dispute over land improved with several small rent houses; the rent houses are mentioned only as property improvements, never analyzed for their legal character or regulation.

Conversion suit over furniture the plaintiff used while operating a rooming house he leased from the defendant landlord; the rooming-house business is background context for a landlord-tenant fixture/conversion and exemplary-damages dispute, not itself analyzed for legality or character.
Wrongful-death suit over a downed power transmission line in a cultivated farm field; involves trespasser/licensee premises-liability doctrine, no letting or lodging issue.

Same underlying opinion as case_id 5238284 (Thurston v. State), reported at a different citation (103 S.W.2d 770 vs. 132 Tex. Crim. 287). Criminal burglary appeal; the boarding house is merely the crime scene, with no discussion of the legality or character of room-letting.

Fire-insurance coverage dispute turning on whether the insureds' own family dwelling became 'unoccupied' under a policy clause during the wife's absence; concerns the insureds' personal occupancy of their own home, not letting of rooms to lodgers or boarders.

Hotel-guest property-theft suit construing Art. 4592 (covering 'hotel, apartment hotel or boarding house keeper') and requiring a jury finding of negligence as to a defective door bolt; the statute is cited only for its civil liability-limitation function, not the legality or character of letting practice.
